_description: Template for weighted, benchmark-ready access patterns. Weights must sum to 1.0. Each pattern has a name, a description, an xarray operation that returns a non-empty result against the store, a weight, the evidence for that weight, and the matching benchmark_runner.py arguments.

dataset.name: DATASET_NAME
dataset._notes: Record coordinate conventions: is lat descending (ds.lat[0] > ds.lat[-1])? Is lon 0-360 or -180-180? Every sel() below must follow them.

patterns.name: spatial_single_timestep
patterns.description: Read a full 2D spatial field at a single timestep. Typical for map visualization and spatial analysis.
patterns.evidence: SOURCE (logs | code review | interview | profiling), or 'ASSUMPTION: <why>'
patterns._notes: Replace VARIABLE and the time value. benchmark_args uses the dimension index of time.

patterns.name: temporal_single_point
patterns.description: Read a full time series at a single spatial location. Typical for trend analysis and station validation.
patterns.evidence: SOURCE (logs | code review | interview | profiling), or 'ASSUMPTION: <why>'
patterns._notes: Write LON in the store's convention (90W is 270 on a 0-360 grid). method='nearest' does not raise an error for a point outside the grid.

patterns.name: spectral_single_point_time
patterns.description: Read across the full spectral/frequency axis at a single spatial location and timestep. Typical for spectral analysis and calibration.
patterns.evidence: SOURCE (logs | code review | interview | profiling), or 'ASSUMPTION: <why>'
patterns._notes: Only relevant for datasets with a spectral or frequency dimension. Remove if not applicable.

patterns.name: diagonal_regional_timeseries
patterns.description: Read a spatial subset across a time range, then aggregate spatially. Typical for regional climate indices and area-averaged statistics.
patterns.evidence: SOURCE (logs | code review | interview | profiling), or 'ASSUMPTION: <why>'
patterns._notes: Slice bounds must follow coordinate order: slice(60, 30) on a descending lat. benchmark_runner.py has no diagonal access mode, so leave benchmark_args null and say so in the report.

metadata._notes: Record how patterns were identified and who approved the weights.
